content.thinking:
I need to fix a search indexing bug where archived projects, issues, and comments remain discoverable.

Search results must reflect live state at all times. A project is discoverable only while live. An issue is discoverable only while its project and itself are live. A comment is discoverable only while its issue, project, and comment are all live. This rule applies through archiving, restoring, and edits.

Restoring a project does not restore issues that were archived separately or with it. Those issues and their comments remain hidden.

A workspace index rebuild must produce exactly the allowed entries for that workspace. It must not touch other workspaces.

content.text: I'll look through the search-index code and how archive, restore, and rebuild update it.

content.thinking: I need to understand the archive and restore flow for projects and issues, and how comments are indexed.

I need to understand list pagination, comment listing, findIssue, project archive behavior, and whether comments have a projectId.

Search visibility depends on the project, issue, and comment all being live. Archived projects hide their issues and comments from search; restoring a project brings back only live issues and comments. Archived issues remain hidden even after the project is restored.

The reindex job must call the existing indexIssue, indexComment, and indexProject functions rather than reimplementing them. It should rebuild every allowed entry across the workspace while skipping archived issues, deleted comments, and archived projects. Stale entries that were incorrectly indexed must be removed. The searchable visibility check belongs in the index writers.

The index writers currently always upsert. They should instead check live status and remove entries that are no longer searchable.

indexComment only receives the comment itself, so it must look up the issue and project to verify their status. indexIssue already has the issue object with its projectId and archivedAt field.

If an issue is archived or its project is archived, the question remains whether to remove only the issue document or also its comments.

The reindex job indexes comments separately. If indexIssue removes an issue but indexComment does not check live status, the comments remain in the index.

Archiving an issue currently only removes the issue document. It must also remove the issue's comments. Archiving a project currently only removes the project. It must also remove all issues and comments belonging to that project.

Restoring a project currently does nothing. The system needs to reindex the restored project along with its live issues and their live comments.

Comments posted after a project is archived still get indexed through comment.created events.

Issue edits after a project archive are reindexed through issue.updated. Those handlers must check visibility.

The search.reindex_requested endpoint only handles issues and always indexes them even if archived.

Search results and their reported totals must follow the visibility rule at all times. Query-time filtering may be needed as a safety net for stale index entries.

The rebuild bug confirms the index itself is dirty. Query-time filtering could mask stale entries, but the fix must correct the index contents directly. I will implement both index maintenance and query filtering if the schema supports joins. Rebuild must delete all existing rows for the organization before rebuilding to purge stale documents.

Deleting by orgId is safe because it only affects the current workspace. The rebuild must explicitly remove non-searchable documents rather than merely upserting visible ones, since skipping archived items would leave stale entries behind. Calling indexIssue and indexComment during rebuild will delete archived issues and comments automatically.

Comments are soft-deleted, not permanently removed. The includeArchived flag causes archived comments to reappear in indexComment and get re-upserted during rebuild. This explains why deleted comments resurfaced in the index.

The rebuild only processes the first page of results. Older issues and comments on later pages were never touched, so stale entries there remain untouched. This explains why older content stayed missing after the rebuild.

The rebuild must walk every project, issue, and comment across all pages. It should also purge index rows for subjects that no longer exist. The goal is to leave only the entries the visibility rule allows.

Checking whether the API supports listing comments for an entire organization or only per issue.

Pagination is broken for large workspaces. The current code fetches only one page of issues and one page of comments, so later pages are skipped entirely.

For stale entries, the plan is to upsert only searchable items. If a project is archived, its document and all related documents should be deleted.

Comments currently lack a projectId, so they cannot be filtered or deleted by project. This is a bug for query filtering.

The plan is to remove the project document when archived, and remove the issue document when archived or its parent project is archived. Callers will handle comment cleanup separately.

A central `syncSubject` function will handle visibility checks and upserts or deletions. Archiving an issue removes its document and all related comments. Archiving a project removes the project document, then recursively deletes all issues and comments under it. Restoring a project re-indexes the project and all live issues and their comments.

Live updates to issues or comments while their parent project is archived must be blocked. The search service should also reindex when comments and projects are created or deleted. Only comment.created and comment.deleted events exist; comment.updated may be needed.

The bug is caused by issue.updated reindexing archived issues. The fix is to check project liveness inside indexIssue before upserting.

`indexComment` will now check the parent issue and project liveness before upserting. If either is archived, it removes the comment from the index. The author notes that storing `projectId` on comments would enable project-scoped search, but changing this field could affect existing filters.

The probeLimit caps the limit at 100.

Pagination must continue through nextCursor until null. Orphan index rows might survive if the cleanup job permanently deletes source rows. The cleanup-archived-job needs inspection.

Comment updates do not emit events.

The bug report concerns issue edits and new comments, not comment updates. Comment body edits will not update the search index because no comment.updated event exists.

Project archiving must remove all issue and comment documents from the index. The project.archived listener should handle this, and subsequent comment.created or issue.updated events must not re-add them because indexIssue and indexComment check project liveliness.

Project restoration reindexes the project along with its live issues and comments.

Archiving an issue removes that issue and its comments from the index.

There is a concern that indexIssue might also delete comments when the issue is not searchable, which would cause reindexing an archived issue to drop its comments.

The project.archived event does not include the list of issues, so the listener must query them. The issue.archived handler should re-read the archived issue and call indexIssue instead of only removing it from the index. This ensures comments are also dropped.

A bulk deletion helper for project-scoped search documents would avoid querying every archived issue individually. However, comment documents currently store projectId as null, so a project-wide deletion would miss them. Storing projectId on comments would fix this but could alter existing test totals.

Comment documents will keep projectId as null. The project archiving flow will list all issues including archived ones, then explicitly delete each issue and its comments by ID. During project restoration, only live issues will be reindexed along with their live comments.

The project itself must be indexed as well.

Archived issues remain hidden after both individual and project archiving. Restoring a project does not revive an issue that was archived independently.

A comment on a live issue stays searchable. An archived comment on a live issue becomes non-searchable, so rebuilds must remove it rather than upsert it.

indexComment should verify the issue is live before upserting a comment. indexIssue must not re-add an archived issue, even if an update event somehow reaches it. The search.reindex_requested handler should use index* for all subject types so visibility checks remove archived documents or delete missing ones.

A reusable `eachPage` helper is being drafted to paginate through rebuild results.

Walking every source row and removing non-visible entries should eliminate stale index rows. The rebuild is scoped to one organization, so orphaned entries from deleted organizations are not a concern. Fully paginated traversal ensures archived comments are still visited even if the issue page was truncated. A hard-deleted issue with an indexed comment is considered unlikely.

Walking every source row and deleting non-visible entries from the index fixes the reported issues. Archived rows still exist in the database, so skipping them during rebuilds removes the stale entries that "came back" or "survived." The pagination fix resolves missing older issues. All deletions and upserts are scoped to the organization ID, ensuring other workspaces remain untouched.

The rebuild should first delete all existing search documents for the organization, then reinsert only the live subjects. This guarantees the index contains exactly the allowed entries and avoids touching other workspaces. Deleting every row first is safe even for large workspaces because the job can load all subject keys into memory.

A brief empty index during rebuild is acceptable because the end state must be correct. The job file comment about handing every row to index writers does not prevent adding an org-scoped wipe, and tests likely verify behavior rather than implementation.

Adding a new repository function is acceptable. The phrase "entries that should not be there survived" likely refers to orphaned index rows left behind when archived rows are deleted without a prior wipe, rather than only the re-added bad entries.

The indexIssue helper will remove an issue from the search index when it is no longer searchable. This lets incremental events clean up stale entries without a full rebuild. The project.archived listener must also deindex descendant issues and comments, since removing only the project document would leave them in the index.

indexIssue will delete all comments for an issue when the issue is no longer searchable. This is safe because reindex calls indexIssue before indexComment, so live comments are re-added afterward and archived comments are already removed.

indexIssue must only delete comments when the issue becomes unsearchable. If it always removed all comments, every live issue edit would drop its comments from search. The helper will check visibility first and only remove comments when the issue is no longer searchable.

Project updates fail to emit events.

Project renames won't update search. The event map lacks a project.updated event, so edits can't be caught. Restore events do fire. For rebuilds, I'll wipe the index before reindexing to keep it exact. Concurrent writes during rebuild are unlikely in this single-threaded app.

Wiping the index before rebuilding is safer than scanning afterward. A failed index would still leave data missing, but that matches current behavior. The deletion will be scoped to the organization ID to avoid touching other workspaces. I'll add a `deleteSearchDocumentsForOrg` repository method.
